bluf: Huge is a New York design and technology company, independent again since 2024, selling brand, digital products, composable commerce, customer experience and AI activation to enterprise brands. It is doing AI at the operating model level: workflow redesign for human and agent work, a MAKE.EXE live AI creative competition returning on Oct 6, and 14+ LinkedIn ads on speed and AI outcomes. Where it is going: absorbing Hero Digital under a Chief Client Officer hired in Nov 2025. The thing a rival should know: all 12 named clients are names only, and its delivery footprint in Medellín, Bogotá and Ho Chi Minh City is on the record.
doing:
Huge positions itself as a human first, AI native design and technology company building brands, digital products, commerce and customer experiences for ambitious brands. In plain words: a digital product and experience builder for enterprise brands that now sells AI operating model work on top of the build. Its headline claim is that it reinvented McDonald's ordering into a multi billion dollar sales channel and holds a 14+ year Google partnership, both quoted as its claims.

The sold mix has one lead line, web and product (scored 3: products and platforms and composable commerce lines, McDonald's ordering, Planet Fitness and Big Green Egg builds), with AI automation the second core line (scored 2: an AI activation line that redesigns workflows around agents and builds AI infrastructure, AI native positioning in the homepage meta). CRO, content, data and measurement and email each score 1 with no evidence note; every media, search and social line scores 0. Services: brand strategy and design, marketing and content, products and platforms, composable commerce, customer experience, AI activation. Proprietary: the Huge LIVE platform, Intelligent Experience (IX) capabilities and MAKE.EXE. No partners are listed.

AI posture: AI activation as workflow and operating model redesign for human and agent work plus AI and data infrastructure, staged publicly through MAKE.EXE. Moves in date order: 2024, the company timeline marks Huge becoming independent again; 2025-11, it hired Lauren DeGeorge, ex Publicis Digital Experience, as Chief Client Officer, and the same release cites its integration with Hero Digital, whose domain redirects to hugeinc.com; 2026-09, six 2026 Creativepool Annual awards including Gold for the PepsiCo rebrand and site; 2026-09, the return of MAKE.EXE, a live AI creative competition in New York on Oct 6. Pricing signals: none. Conspicuously absent for a builder of its kind: any SEO, AI search or feed and schema line on the commerce work it ships, and any media line.
clients:
The record types the client as enterprise across quick service restaurants, technology, media and entertainment, fitness, healthcare, sports, financial technology, luxury retail and consumer products. The home market is the US, with New York headquarters and offices in London, Chicago, Philadelphia, Austin, Atlanta, the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Detroit, Washington, D.C., Toronto, Medellín, Bogotá and Ho Chi Minh City.

The needs read lists 12 clients, 0 observed and 12 named only: 10 case study pages, 1 slug and 1 award entry with no work described in the record. McDonald's, Google, NBCUniversal, Planet Fitness, CoinTracker, Darling Ingredients, Big Green Egg, UNC Health, LPGA and Hublot are case study pages, Candescent a slug, and PepsiCo an award entry, the Creativepool award, Gold for its rebrand and site. No mix can be computed. The needs are inferred from what the agency leads with: web build and platform first, brand and creative behind it. The capability notes cite McDonald's ordering, Planet Fitness and Big Green Egg as builds, a web build need observed only as notes, and the PepsiCo entry names a rebrand and site.

Three clients are shared: Google sits on the books of instrument, r-ga, dept, media-monks, akqa and brave-bison; PepsiCo on pmg and vaynermedia; McDonald's on epsilon. The whole book is names only (12 of 12), which the record flags as a question to ask its clients.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places Huge best for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), driven by AI automation and data and measurement, with no headwind judgment. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that these enterprise brands buy operating model and agent workflow work next, the AI activation line, more than new builds.
house:
Say and do: the Radar ran no house test on Huge, since neither core line (web and product, AI automation) carries one, so integrity is null and no gap was flagged. It runs 11 Google ads in the Transparency Center, 0 in the last 30 days, 4 text, 1 image and 6 video, last shown 2026-08-26, under Huge LLC. LinkedIn: 14+ company ads and 0 thought leader ads, a floor since more result pages exist; one sample reads The longer you plan, the further behind you fall, we move fast; another, Most AI investments promise transformation and deliver complexity.

The site runs on Next.js with GTM, sixsense and OneTrust; sixsense is the ABM stack, with no social pixels and no testing tools detected. Sitemap: 93 URLs, 11 updated in 90 days and the same 11 in 365, a recent but thin cadence. No llms.txt, no AI crawlers blocked, 0 AI URLs, for a company whose homepage meta says AI native.
market:
The Horus read scores Huge at a tailwind index of 27.6, band Favored, 86th percentile; integrity is null because no line was tested. Best placed for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net 0.486) and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net 0.3, AI automation at +2), with no headwind judgment at all. Best fit is The Commons Rebuilt at 50/100. Moves: partial on P6 (agent operators) and P7 (owned audience hedges), unknown on P5 pricing, absent on P1 and P2, P3, P4 and P8 not applicable.

The Monsoon read: index 64.6, band Onshore wind, 83rd percentile; migration 73.1 against displacement 56.1, with an observed hub office term of 12 and an enterprise term of -5. The verdict puts 61 of the index on the sold mix, web and product (30) and AI automation (9), and the delivery footprint is observed, not inferred: Medellín, Bogotá and Ho Chi Minh City are listed offices, and the shore split is 62% South and Southeast Asia and 31% Latin America. No onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the footprint against the price. Huge lists delivery offices in Medellín, Bogotá and Ho Chi Minh City, the Monsoon read puts migration at 73.1, and it publishes no pricing model. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival with an onshore delivery pitch and an outcome priced build offer can contest enterprise accounts paying New York rates for work the record shows can be delivered from those hubs. Falsifier: Huge publishing where its builds are staffed, or a price model tied to shipped outcomes.

Second, proof: 12 of 12 clients are names only, so the question for McDonald's, Planet Fitness or UNC Health is what the engagement delivered beyond the claim. Third, the shoppers: Google already buys from six other tracked agencies (instrument, r-ga, dept, media-monks, akqa, brave-bison) and PepsiCo from pmg and vaynermedia, so both are a roughly even chance to be contested on a single workstream. Fourth, the machine readable layer: a commerce builder with no feed, schema or entity work and no AI search line leaves the layer answer engines consume unclaimed on every site it ships, and its own site has no llms.txt, a gap against an AI native claim.
